title: Sardines by Chris Grace at New York Theatre Workshop #chrisgrace #chr...
transcript: Sardines is a solo piece that strikes the perfect mix between the personal and the universal. Written and performed by Chris Grace, it's a self-proclaimed “comedy about death” in which Chris walks us through a family portrait full of people who have passed away. At just 52 years old, he's already lost pretty much all of the closest people in his life. It's almost unfathomable, really — it's the kind of situation that anyone in the audience would hope doesn't ever become their reality. It's that fear, for lack of a better term, that makes the show both personal and universal. It is still a comedy, however, and there's something comforting in seeing someone who's gone through what they've gone through standing on the other side and in seemingly good spirits. This piece really invites you in, cutting the tension with an audience rendition of a Rihanna song or asking you to imagine all of the projected images on a nonexistent screen. The immediacy goes hand in hand with the universality, and it makes all of the emotions, the highs and the lows of the piece, hit just the right amount. Sardines is running at New York Theatre Workshop in their first In The Bricks Festival. With that, another program for my collection.
